findings_addressed: TC-97 — THE PYTEST HEADER NOW PRINTS `configfile:`, AND IT IS NOT A LEAK. MEASURED: header reads `rootdir: <wt>/scripts/sbom-survey` + `configfile: pyproject.toml`. The configfile is THIS DIRECTORY'S OWN pyproject.toml — an unavoidable consequence of design §6 requiring the file at scripts/sbom-survey/, which IS an ancestor of scripts/sbom-survey/tests. NOTHING IS INHERITED: probed via a pytest plugin, config.inipath == <wt>/scripts/sbom-survey/pyproject.toml, config.rootpath == <wt>/scripts/sbom-survey, config.inicfg == {} (EMPTY), config.getini('pythonpath') == []. The mechanism is explicit in the installed pytest source (_pytest/config/findpaths.py::locate_config): a pyproject.toml carrying no [tool.pytest.ini_options] makes load_config_dict_from_file return None, and the function then falls through to `if found_pyproject_toml is not None: return found_pyproject_toml.parent, found_pyproject_toml, {}, []` — i.e. the file becomes the ROOTDIR ANCHOR with an EMPTY config dict. src/python/pyproject.toml is not on the ancestor chain and is never reached. TC-105 / §7 BOUNDARY-DEFECT SWEEP — 'a criterion graded against a helper while the integration boundary that must call it goes ungraded' produced 9 of Slice 31's 12 review findings. Slice 32 is the mirror image of that: an implementation can satisfy a helper's contract while the boundary does not do the thing. EVERY ITEM the prompt listed was swept, and each was verified TWICE — once by reading/writing the code, and once EMPIRICALLY by deliberately breaking it and confirming the frozen suite goes RED (the 14-mutation sweep below). (1) run_survey takes its manifests ONLY from discover_manifests(): grep across scripts/sbom-survey/sbom_survey/ for os.walk / rglob / iglob / glob. / import glob / .iterdir() / scandir returns ONLY docstring and comment hits, and there is no literal 'python/' path in code. (2) run_survey calls published.latest() ONCE PER COMPONENT — instrumented a counting source over the real repo: 773 components, 773 calls, 704 distinct (ecosystem, name) keys. (3) Exclusion and tiering come ONLY from the injected/loaded TierMap: the string 'dev/release/fixtures/' appears in the repository's code path nowhere — only in tiers.toml (data) and in prose. (4) Tier matching is longest-prefix-wins via max(len(prefix)) over EVERY matching rule, so it is order-independent by construction; two distinct prefixes of equal length cannot both prefix one string, so the winner is unique. Duplicate prefixes raise DuplicateTierPrefixError (a TierRuleFileError/ValueError, deliberately NOT an UntieredManifestError) from load_tier_map(), naming the prefix. (5) The BOM's fathomdb:tier is derived from the DECLARING MANIFEST's rule verdict — independently recomputed over the real repo: 42 components carry exactly one origin, 0 tier mismatches against TierMap.classify(origin).tier. (6) `direct` is DEFINED as 'has at least one tracked declaring manifest', so a direct component with no fathomdb:declared-in origin is impossible by construction — verified: 0 depth/origin contradictions across 773 components. (7) The default timestamp is a fixed epoch produced by ONE function, resolve_timestamp(), shared by run_survey and the CLI; argparse's --now default is None PRECISELY so the parser cannot inject a wall-clock stamp behind the survey's back, and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH keeps working as §5.8's override. There is no datetime.now() / utcnow() / time.time() / date.today() call anywhere in the package. (8) write_reports() PRODUCES the artifact shape rather than projecting a poorer one — mutation M9 proves the criterion bites. (9) sbom_survey.cyclonedx.validate() really runs the schema: it returns None for the emitted document and a diagnostic for the known-invalid control, verified out of band as well as by AC-SBOM-10.

DESIGN AMBIGUITY RESOLVED 1/3 — THE TIER OF A COMPONENT REACHABLE FROM SEVERAL MANIFESTS. §5.3 fixes the tier of a MANIFEST; it does not say what tier a COMPONENT takes when it is declared by more than one manifest, or when it is a transitive with no declaring manifest at all. RESOLUTION, forced by the frozen oracle: a component's tier candidates are the tiers of its DECLARING MANIFESTS when it has any, and otherwise the tiers of the LOCKFILES that resolved it; the highest-priority tier wins (shipped > dev-tooling > eval-only, i.e. TIER_VOCABULARY order). With exactly one origin this reduces to that origin's tier, which is what AC-SBOM-11 requires. NOTE the consequence, stated rather than hidden: `packaging` is both a transitive of the shipped src/python/uv.lock AND a direct dependency of this dev-tooling mini-project, so it tiers dev-tooling. Including the lockfile tier in the candidate set would make it `shipped` and would then FAIL AC-SBOM-11, since it carries exactly one origin. Origins-win is therefore the rule the frozen oracle demands, not a preference.

DESIGN AMBIGUITY RESOLVED 2/3 — WHICH VERSIONS A MANIFEST DECLARATION ATTACHES TO. §5.5 defines direct-ness by NAME ('the package name appears in a dependency table'), while components are identified per (ecosystem, name, version). A declaration is therefore attached to every component sharing its (ecosystem, name) — with pypi names canonicalized per PEP 503, so a pyproject.toml saying `PyYAML` and a lock saying `pyyaml` are one package. A declared name with NO matching lock entry materializes an UNRESOLVED component: version omitted, purl without an @version segment, and fathomdb:resolution='unresolved'. That case is real on this repo (maturin, networkx, numpy, pyyaml, scipy are declared in src/python/pyproject.toml's optional groups but absent from uv.lock) and is exactly the shape test_cyclonedx.py and test_report.py were written to accommodate — the prompt flagged that `fathomdb:resolution == 'unresolved'` is required by the tests and not spelled out in §5.

DESIGN AMBIGUITY RESOLVED 3/3 — THE fathomdb:edge-kind = 'resolved' TAG. §5.5 says lock-derived edges are tagged 'resolved', but CycloneDX `dependencies` entries carry no property bag, so an edge cannot literally hold one. RESOLUTION: the tag is emitted as a COMPONENT property on every component whose outgoing edges came from a lockfile, and the real normal/dev/build kinds — which only manifest-derived declarations carry — travel in staleness.json's `declared_in[].kind`. The §5.5 limitation is thereby recorded rather than papered over.

IMPLEMENTATION CHOICE WORTH FLAGGING — THE DOCUMENT IS BUILT BY THE LIBRARY, NOT HAND-ROLLED. §5.7 makes cyclonedx-python-lib load-bearing twice: to 'build and serialize' the document, and to supply the schema validator. Both uses are taken. sbom_survey/cyclonedx.py assembles a real Bom / Component / Dependency model and serializes with JsonV1Dot6, so the emitted `$schema` / `bomFormat` / `specVersion` / key ordering / dependency array come from the upstream serializer, and the hand-rolled-JSON failure mode REQ-6 exists to prevent is structurally avoided. Determinism was checked against that decision rather than assumed: the serializer sorts components, properties and dependencies, the serialNumber is a UUIDv5 over the sorted bom-ref set (never uuid4), the timestamp is the fixed epoch, and two independent runs are byte-identical.
